title: The Locker of the quarry
premise: In the quarry town of Halloway Bend, the school's 'Locker of the Quarry' has granted anonymous wishes for a century — wishes written in ink that shouldn't exist. When Mara Thornbury, the town's only out kid, starts receiving notes addressed to him by name, he discovers the Locker's ghost is actually the trapped memory of a boy erased from the town's records in 1948 for the same reason Mara stands out. To free him before the quarry floods on Homecoming night, Mara must force the town to speak the erased boy's name aloud and reckon with the injustice that built their tradition. The Locker opens one last time, the ghost dissolves into ordinary ink, and Mara writes his own name in it — finally, permanently, himself.
about_author: Kestrel Marchetti grew up in a fading mill town where local legends were treated more seriously than library books, an obsession that never left. They write young adult stories about small towns with big secrets and the kids brave enough to say their own names out loud.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the first day of senior year, Mara finds a note in his locker addressed to him by name, written in ink that shifts color and can't be smudged. More notes follow, referencing memories only he holds. The emotional beat is wary wonder: after fifteen years of careful invisibility, something sees him completely — and that terrifies as much as it thrills.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with interludes from the ghost's 1948 diary pages. Researching the Locker's origin, Mara finds a photograph with one face scratched out and a class roster with a burned hole where a name should be. The notes begin answering his questions before he asks them. The beat is dread deepening into resolve: someone was erased for being like him, and the town did the erasing.

chapters.title: Homecoming Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mara and his best friend Denny, who has secretly reported the notes to the principal. The quarry flood is scheduled for dawn; the ghost's presence is fraying, notes arriving half-written. Mara confronts Denny, then the school board, and is stonewalled. The beat is betrayal and defiance: justice outside the law means doing it himself, tonight, with no permission.

chapters.title: Say His Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the flooded quarry's edge, Mara reads the recovered diary aloud over the PA system, forcing nine hundred people to hear Elian Marsh's name and crime: being a boy who loved boys in 1948. The Locker splits open; Elian's memory chooses dissolution over vengeance, leaving one final note for Mara. The beat is grief transmuted into belonging — Mara signs his own name in the last of the impossible ink.
